newsitem.title: JAPAN: Honda mulls moving Accord output to Japan from US.
newsitem.headline: Honda mulls moving Accord output to Japan from US.

text.p: Honda Motor Co Ltd said on Thursday it is considering transferring production of its Accord Wagon recreational vehicle from its U.S. factory in Ohio to Japan as early as next autumn.

Demand for the vehicle is growing in Japan, and Honda maintains a policy that its products are better produced where they are sold, a company spokesman said. Annual production of the Accord Wagon at the Ohio plant is about 70,000. The plant exported 45,000 of the vehicles to Japan in 1995.

Business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported on Thursday that Honda would increase production of other models at the Ohio plant to offset the decision to stop making Accord Wagons there. It said sales of the models were stronger in Japan than in the United States.
Honda plans to stop exporting its medium-sized sedan Acura TL to the United States in 1998 and start making a similar model tailored to the U.S. market in Ohio, the paper said.

Toyota Motor unit Toyota Motor Manufacturing Kentucky in Georgetown, Kentucky, stopped making the Scepter station wagon in June because of poor U.S. demand. Toyota sold 12,844 U.S.-made Scepter station wagons in Japan in calendar 1995 and 6,681 from January to September this year.
